pairs.question: Utrum superbiorem te pecunia facit an quod te imperator consulit?
pairs.answer: Moriar, ni, quae tua gloria est, puto te malle a Caesare consuli quam inaurari.
pairs.derivation: Disjunctive interrogative (utrum...an) addressed to Trebatius, immediately answered by Cicero himself in the next sentence. Dropped the framing address 'Audi, Testa mi:' before the question. Answer is the single contiguous sentence to the first full stop ('...inaurari.'), which resolves the either/or by stating Cicero supposes Trebatius prefers being consulted by Caesar (the latter option) to being gilded; what follows ('Si vero utrumque est, quis te feret praeter me...') is a further rhetorical turn, not part of the answer.
